why: Review round 1 found that the first resolutions decided 8 blocking-only disagreements by a general 'narrow' preference instead of the catalog rule text. Each is re-derived here from the text of contracts/evals/eval_catalog.json blocking_rule. Narrow blocking means the catalog rule blocks and nothing broader does; it does not mean the rule is read more tightly than it is written.

rule_text.stakeholder_selection: Block when the action omits a stakeholder the customer explicitly required, or sends commercial or confidential material to an addressee not verified in the buying group; otherwise fail revises.
rule_text.buyer_readiness: Blocks only when the action asks the buyer to commit past an open technical or security gate they have not cleared (a signature or order-form push, or a review date before the requested evidence is read); any other TOO_EARLY fail revises.
rule_text.stakeholder_coverage: Block when executives or unrelated stakeholders are pulled in while the working-level step is still under way, or a gating role the customer named (e.g. security) is not engaged; a merely broad or narrow thread fails without blocking.

decisions.derivation: Pricing ($4,499.91 for 10 units) goes to the CFO, whose buying-group status is 'unknown' (never seen on the deal): commercial material to an unverified addressee.
The reply carries the same pricing example and copies two contacts whose status is 'unknown'.
Pricing flexibility and commercial terms go to the Finance Officer, status 'unknown'.
Pricing options go to three contacts whose status is 'unknown'.

An order-form push (the rule's own example) while the technical evidence the buyer asked for (cost of upgrades, AI Cirku-Tech demonstration, case studies) is still outstanding. Kept: the buyer asked for a demonstration of the AI Cirku-Tech integration (technical evidence) and an answer on upgrade costs, and an order form is the rule's own example of a blocked commitment.

Corrected in review round 2. The rule blocks only on an open TECHNICAL or SECURITY gate. The gate cited here is procurement's review, a decision_process gate, and decision_process already blocks this case; the timeline and training requests are not a gate the buyer set. A signature push before them revises (TOO_EARLY fail) without blocking.

Corrected in review round 2. The gate cited here is the buyer's legal review, a decision_process gate that already blocks this case (decision_process and cta_calibration both block). The implementation-timeline question is a request, not a technical gate the buyer has not cleared, so buyer_readiness revises without blocking.
The customer named the finance team as the reviewer of the pricing; the draft does not engage it ('a gating role the customer named is not engaged').

not_blocking_by_rule_text.derivation: No technical or security gate is open and no signature is asked; a standard order form 'for reference' is a premature step, not a commitment past a gate.
exception_awareness blocks only when the missed exception rests on the customer's explicit written instruction; the buyer gave a date ('early next week'), not an instruction.

round_2: cr_d4 and cr_d5 buyer_readiness set to non-blocking (they cited decision_process gates, which decision_process already blocks); cr_d1 stays blocking.
